Using Standard Method for the Examination 
 of Water and Waste Water, (209 A) 15th Edition

A well mixed sample is evaporated in a weighed dish 
 and dried to constant weight in an oven at 103 to 105oC. 
 The 
 increase in weight over that of the empty dish represents the total residue. 
 Although the results may not represent the weight of actual dissolved and 
 suspended solids in waste water samples, the determination is useful for plant 
 control. In some instances, correlation may be improved by adding 1 N sodium 
 hydroxide (NaOH) to waste water samples with a pH below 4.3 and maintaining the 
 pH of 4.3 during evaporation. Correct final calculation for added sodium.

 control Head sector.

Chemical
Technical Procedure
TitleTotal Residue Dried at 103-105oC
Procedure
Using Standard Method for the Examination 
 of Water and Waste Water, (209 A) 15th Edition
Introduction
A well mixed sample is evaporated in a weighed dish 
 and dried to constant weight in an oven at 103 to 105oC. 
 The 
 increase in weight over that of the empty dish represents the total residue. 
 Although the results may not represent the weight of actual dissolved and 
 suspended solids in waste water samples, the determination is useful for plant 
 control. In some instances, correlation may be improved by adding 1 N sodium 
 hydroxide (NaOH) to waste water samples with a pH below 4.3 and maintaining the 
 pH of 4.3 during evaporation. Correct final calculation for added sodium.
The first draft initiated by chem. Khaled Abd 
 El Salam Mohamed tested by chem. Esam Abd ElAziz, reviewed by general manager 
 chemist Mohamed Kamal, revised by quality control chemist Wael A. Tantawy at EDEPC, 
 approved by eng. Mokhtar Maddy: head sector of Abu Sultan PS,
 and 
 certified by accountant Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman; general director of Admin.& 
 Financial quality control, and supervisor of EDEPC inspection & quality 
 control Head sector.
Significance
Determination of total residue in water of a well 
mixed sample by evaporation and drying 
at oven at 103-105oC to a constant weight. The increase in weight 
represents the total residue.
Interferences
Exclude large floating particles or submerged agglomerates of nonhomogenous 
materials from the sample. Dispers visible floating oil and grease with a 
blender before withdrawing a sample portion for analysis.
Safety Precautions
Store 
 sample in glass bottles.
The reagent 
 used must be of sufficiently high purity to permit its use without 
 lessening the accuracy of determination.

Tools and 
Equipment
Apparatus
a) Evaporating dishs- Dishs of 100 ml capacity made of
porcelain, 90-mm diam.
high silica glas,
Platinum- Generally satisfactory for all purposes.

b) Muffle furnace for for operation at 550oC 
 50oC,
c) Desiccator- Provided with a desiccant containing a color 
 indicator of moisture concentration,
d) Analytical balance- 200 g capacity, capable of 
 weighing to 0.1 mg
e) Drying oven- For operation at 103 -105oC 
 and
f) Steam bath.
Reagents
Distilled water.
Work to be Carried out
Ignite clean evaporating dish at 550oC 50oC 
 for1 hr in a muffle furnace.
Cool, desiccate, weigh and store dish in desiccator until 
 ready for use.
Transfer a measured volume of sample to preweighed dish and 
 evaporate to dryness on a steam bath or in a drying oven. Choose a sample volume that will yield a 
 residue between 2.5 mg and 200 mg. Volume required may be estimated from 
 conductivity. If necessary, add successive sample portions to the same dish. 
 When evaporating in a drying oven, lower temperature to approximately 2oC 
 below boiling to prevent splattering.
Dry evaporated sample for at least 1 hr at 103 to 105oC.
Cool dish in desiccator to balance temperature and weigh.
Repeat cycle of drying at 103 to 105oC, cooling, 
 desiccating and weighing until a constant weight is obtained, or until weight 
 loss is less than 4% of previous weight.
Calculation
(A-B) X 1000
Total Residue mg/L = -------------------------
Sample Volume, ml.
Where
A = weight of sample + dish, mg and
B = weight of dish, mg.
